**Load Packages**

```{r, message = F}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(ggridges)
library(patchwork)
```

# Problem 1

**Loading Data**

```{r}
data = ("ny_noaa")
```

**Counting Missing Values**

```{r, results = "hide"}
ny_noaa |>
  summarize(
    missing_id = sum(is.na(id)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100,
    missing_date = sum(is.na(date)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100,
    missing_prcp = sum(is.na(prcp)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100,
    missing_snow = sum(is.na(snow)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100,
    missing_snwd = sum(is.na(snwd)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100,
    missing_tmax = sum(is.na(tmax)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100,
    missing_tmin = sum(is.na(tmin)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100
  )
```

This NOAA data set has `r nrow(ny_noaa)` observations anf `r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables. The variables in the data set include  `id`, `date`, `prcp`, `snow`, `snwd`, `tmax`, and `tmin`, which provides information on weather station ID numbers, the date of observation, precipitation (in tenths of mm), snowfall (mm), snow depth(mm), and the maximum and minimum temperatures (in tenths of degrees C). Since there are many different weather stations, and that each weather station may only collect a subset of the variables, the data set has a lot of missing data. Upon investigation, it is clear that the maximum and minimum temperature data is extensively missing, with `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$tmax)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100` % of observations missing for maximum temperatures and `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$tmin)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100`% for minimum temperatures. Snow depth also had a good amount of missing observations, with `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$snwd)) / nrow(ny_noaa) * 100`% of observations missing. 

**Problem 1 Questions:**

- Do some data cleaning. Create separate variables for year, month, and day. Ensure observations for temperature, precipitation, and snowfall are given in reasonable units. For snowfall, what are the most commonly observed values? Why?

**Cleaning the data set**

```{r}
ny_noaa_df = 
  ny_noaa |> 
  mutate(
    month = lubridate::month(date), 
    year = lubridate::year(date), 
    day = lubridate::day(date), 
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10, 
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10, 
    prcp = prcp / 10 
  )
```

**Most Common Snowfalls**

```{r}
ny_noaa_df |>
  count(snow) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  head()
```

The most commonly observed snowfall value was 0mm. This makes sense since that snowfall does not occur on most of the days of a given year. The second most commonly observed snowfall value was NA, which indicates that there was a substantial number of missing snowfall observations. Other commonly observed values included 25mm, 13mm, 51mm and 76mm. When converted into inches, these values round to approximately 1, 0.5, 2, and 3 inches, which would make sense for New York City. 

**Two Panel Plot Showing Max. Temperature in January and July**

- Make a two-panel plot showing the average max temperature in January and in July in each station across years. Is there any observable / interpretable structure? Any outliers?

```{r, warning = F, message = F}
temperature_df =
ny_noaa_df |>
  filter(month == 1 | month == 7) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_tmax))
```

```{r}
temperature_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15, size = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month,
             labeller = as_labeller(c("1" = "January", "7" = "July"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in January and July Over Time",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  ) 
```

As expected, the average maximum temperatures were much higher in July than in January because of seasonal temperature differences between the Summer and the Winter. January temperatures generally range from approximately -10°C to 10°C. July temperatures are generally range from 20°C and 32°C. Based on these two panels and where the points lie, there is visibly no overlap between the two months. January temperatures seem to fluctuate more across time, while July temperatures are relatively more consistent. There are a few outliers. For the month of July, in the late 1980s, the station captured an average maximum temperature of around 14°C, which is much lower than other recorded observations. As for January, there is an outlier in the early 1980s that captured a maximum temperature around -14°C. 

**Plot Showing Tmax vs. Tmin for Full Data Set** 

- Make a two-panel plot showing (i) tmax vs tmin for the full dataset (note that a scatterplot may not be the best option); and (ii) make a plot showing the distribution of snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 separately by year.

```{r, warning = F}
tmaxvstmin_plot = 
ny_noaa_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex() +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs. Minimum Temperature", 
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)", 
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)" 
  )

tmaxvstmin_plot
```

**Plot showing the distribution of snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 separately by year**

```{r, warning = F, message = F}
snowfalldis_plot =
  ny_noaa_df |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = snow, y = factor(year))) +
  geom_density_ridges(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Year"
  ) 

snowfalldis_plot
```

**Combining the two plots into a two-panel plot**

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=12, warning = F}
tmaxvstmin_plot / snowfalldis_plot
```
